newsitem.title: USA: Continental expects final approval of BA-AA deal.
newsitem.headline: Continental expects final approval of BA-AA deal.

text.p: Continental Airlines Chairman Gordon Bethune on Thursday said he expects the proposed alliance between British Airways and American Airlines to ultimately be approved by British and U.S. regulators.
But Bethune said he expects regulators to force additional concessions from the airlines to ease competitive concerns on both sides of the Atlantic over the code-sharing pact.

"This thing appears to be headed for fruition," Bethune said. "I can't see this thing being prevented, but I certainly can see it being reconstituted so that we don't lose and the consumer doesn't lose."

Continental in a filing with the Office of Fair Trading, Britain's competition advisory panel, said regulators must take steps to keep the alliance between British Airways Plc and AMR Corp's American Airlines from "strangling competition" in trans-Atlantic routes.
"What you've got here is a merger under the guise of an alliance," he said of the BA-AA code-sharing pact.

The airlines, the top two carriers in the Heathrow-New York market, would control more than 60 percent of the seats between the two countries, and 70 percent of seats from Heathrow to the United States, Continental said.

To compete, the Houston-based airline said it alone would need 140 of 168 weekly landing slots at London's Heathrow airport to be relinquished by the two rival carriers, along with adequate gates and counter space at the giant airport.
Continental would schedule six daily flights from Newark, N.J., three from Houston and one from Cleveland to compete with the BA-AA alliance, Bethune said.

In addition to protests filed with the British government, U.S. regulators are expected to scrutinize the deal's competitive impact, particularly on trans-Atlantic flights between New York and London, he said.
"This is round one of what may be a protracted battle," Bethune said.
